description: Run the last build of a project for a board (build.start's output) in QEMU: lcgamboa's fork when it is built (ESP32 and C3 through its library, so I2C buses answer no address), else Espressif's prebuilt QEMU. There is no network. Only ESP32, ESP32-S3 and ESP32-C3 boards are simulated; others are workbench-only and refused. Returns a subscription: sim.output carries UART0, sim.frame the virtual RGB panel once firmware draws on it, sim.pins the project's pins, sim.exited says when QEMU stopped. sim.write and sim.reset act on it; core.unsubscribe stops QEMU, as does closing the connection. With debug: true, QEMU starts paused with its GDB stub on loopback and the core attaches the Arduino core's GDB to the build's ELF; debug.* methods and debug.stopped, debug.running and debug.exited events then work on the same subscription. The simulator is firmware-level: no Wi-Fi radio, no attached parts.

engine.description: The QEMU it runs on: lcgamboa's fork once the setup step has built it, else Espressif's prebuilt QEMU.

pins.description: GPIOs the project's build uses (from the library) that this simulation bridges: their changes come as sim.pins, and sim.setPin drives them. Empty where there is no pin access: the S3, and Espressif's QEMU.
